description: Discriminator: the same COMMITTED-reply scenario as claim C1, but with the recovering replica promoted to leader (IsLeader true and a maxRecvBallot above its ballot base), so makeBallot raises the new ballot past what it has seen. Prefix: the peer's record is prepared as COMMITTED with a real PUT command, the recovering replica holds a default record, and the harness drives the Prepare/PrepareReply resolution, the phase-1 restart, the accept round and the commit broadcast. Controls: the seed event prints is_leader, max_recv_ballot, the seed ballot and the self VBallot, so the variant's ballot arithmetic is visible.

harness.description: In-package Go test building two real Replica values and delivering Prepare/PrepareReply through their real Marshal/Unmarshal form.
semantic_changes: harness-only scaffolding: two Replica values are constructed in-package, per-peer buffers replace the transport, and recovery is entered directly through startRecoveryForInstance; handlers are unmodified
variant: the recovering replica has IsLeader true and maxRecvBallot set above its ballot base, modelling the replica the master promoted after it had already seen traffic

legality.derivation: The variant's only additions are the deployment flag the master sets and a ballot history, both of which the sources establish.
legality.applicability: N=3, Thrifty, promoted-leader variant, one COMMITTED reply and one default record.
unresolved: the real ballot history is modelled as one maxRecvBallot value

grounding.derivation: The resolution event is the completed recovery decision for the instance: it records whether the committed vector was adopted, the resulting local status and which message the recoverer emitted.
grounding.applicability: Resolution reached with the prerequisite reply present for the same instance identity.

grounding.derivation: The outcome event is read after the whole recovery path has been driven, so it reports the vector the recoverer actually committed and the vector the peer already had for the same instance.
grounding.applicability: The recovery ran for the same instance and completed the rounds it started.

grounding.derivation: The event records the committed command held by each replica after the recovery's Commit broadcast, so it tests whether the disagreement produced by the resolution survives propagation. The binding is the resolution that produced the vector being propagated.
grounding.applicability: The recoverer committed the instance and the Commit reached the other two replicas.

observable_properties.description: A completed recovery resolution in which a reply reported the instance COMMITTED must adopt that committed vector.
If the recovering replica ends up committing the instance, the command it commits must be the command the replica that already committed the same instance holds.
After the recovery's commit broadcast, every replica that holds the instance committed must hold the same committed command.

uncertainties: The harness prepares the peer's COMMITTED record directly; a full history is not constructed.
The outcome is observed for one instance and one recovery attempt; later Commit propagation to other replicas is not driven.
The third property observes the records the handlers hold after the broadcast; it does not execute the state machines, so the applied-state consequence is left open.
